comment.body:
You're right, filtering after the query was wrong. The indexer returned a page of `limit` results and the handler removed the linked issues from that page afterwards, so the dropdown got fewer results than the page size, or none at all when the newest matches were all already linked. It didn't expose anything extra, it just returned too little.

I took the parameter out of the generic search endpoints and added a dedicated one next to `dependency/add` and `dependency/delete`: `GET /{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/dependency/candidates?q=`. It needs the same permission as adding a dependency, and the backend now decides what the dropdown used to put in the URL: this repo only or every repo the user can read, depending on `ALLOW_CROSS_REPOSITORY_DEPENDENCIES`, and issues, pulls or both, depending on what the user can read in this repo.

For the page size it does what you described: it asks the indexer for `limit + count(excluded)` results, drops the issue and the issues linked to it, and returns the first `limit` of what is left. None of the indexers can exclude a list of IDs (meilisearch would also need `id` as a filterable attribute), and this works the same way for all of them. The dropdown only ever loads the first page, so the endpoint has no `page` parameter. It also drops issues from repos the user reaches through a team without the issues or pulls unit, since `AddDependency` refuses those anyway.

The new integration test covers the exclusions, a full page when the newest matches are the excluded ones, cross-repo on and off, a private repo the user can't read, and a user without write access. The e2e test now goes through the new endpoint.

issue.title: Run PrepareForIndexTests on Windows
issue.body:
Run the three skipped `PrepareForIndexTests` on Windows by matching manifest node paths with the host path separator.

### Motivation:

`testPrepare`, `testPrepareNoLazy` and `testEnableTestingReleaseConfiguration` were skipped on Windows with "coreCommands.count = 0 instead of 1. Possibly related to #8511".

The tests find the compile command for a module by checking whether an output node path ends with a string such as `"debug/Core.build/Core.swiftmodule"`. On Windows the node paths use backslashes. The node for that module is:

```
\path\to\build\x86_64-unknown-windows-msvc\debug\Core.build\Core.swiftmodule
```

so the `/` suffix never matches and the filters come back empty. The build plan itself is fine; only the matching in the test is POSIX-specific.

The same pattern also hid a problem in `testEnableTestingDebugConfiguration`, which is not skipped. It asserts that no command matching `"/lib.swiftmodule"` has a certain flag. On Windows nothing matched at all, so the test passed without checking anything.

### Modifications:

- Add a private `hostPath(_:)` helper in the test file that replaces `/` with `\` on Windows and returns the string unchanged elsewhere.
- Use it for every path match in the file (`debug/Core.build/Core.swiftmodule`, `debug/Modules-tool/SwiftSyntax.swiftmodule`, `-tool.build/`, `/lib.swiftmodule`).
- Remove the three `XCTSkipOnWindows` calls.

No product code changes.

### Result:

All six `PrepareForIndexTests` run and pass on Windows, and `testEnableTestingDebugConfiguration` now actually finds the command it checks. No change on macOS or Linux.

How I checked it:

GitHub Actions `windows-2022` with `nightly-6.4.x`, building with the bootstrapped `swift-build` like the PR workflow (`swift run -Xlinker /ignore:4217 --configuration release swift-build --build-tests --scratch-path .tests`, then `swift-test --skip-build --filter PrepareForIndexTests`). The first runs were on a fork-only branch that also carried the swift-system and `import Foundation` changes that have since landed on `main` (#10643, #10682).

issue.title: Run GitRepositoryTests.testRawRepository on Windows
issue.body:
Run `GitRepositoryTests.testRawRepository` on Windows by leaving the non-portable working-tree files out of the extraction.

### Motivation:

Fixes #8385. `TestRepo.tgz` contains a checked-out `funny-names` directory with files named `a\b`, `a"b`, `a\nb` and similar. `tar.exe` can't create those on Windows ("Invalid argument"), so the extraction step fails and the test has been skipped there.

The test only reads `funny-names` through the object database (`readCommit`, `readTree` on commit `a7b19a7`). It never touches the working-tree copies.

### Modifications:

- On Windows, extract the archive with `--exclude "*/funny-names/*"`, with a short comment saying why.
- Remove the `XCTSkipOnWindows` for #8385. The skip for #8564 (`skipSelfHostedCI: true`) stays, since that hang is a separate problem.

### Result:

The test runs on Windows outside the self-hosted CI. No change on other platforms.

How I checked it:

- macOS: `tar -x --exclude '*/funny-names/*'` on the archive, then `git ls-tree a7b19a7` still lists `README.txt`, `funny-names` and `subdir`, and `1.0` and `main` resolve to the same commit.
- Windows (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`, `tar.exe`): the current command fails with `Can't create ... funny-names\a\b: Invalid argument`. The new command extracts cleanly, and the same values the test asserts come back from git: `main` equals `1.0^{commit}`, the initial commit `a8b9fcbf...` and tree `9d463c3b...`, and the three entries of the `a7b19a7` tree.

I couldn't run the Swift test itself on Windows. A plain build of `main` there currently fails in the `swift-build` checkout (`FileDescriptor.OpenOptions` has no member `closeOnExec`), which also shows up in other PR runs today, so I checked the extraction and the git reads directly instead.

issue.body:
When writing a download fails, icloudpd logs the same text whatever the error is:

```
ERROR    IOError while writing file to .../IMG_6731.JPG. You might have run out of disk space, or the file might be too large for your OS. Skipping this file...
```

In #1288 the disk wasn't full: the Nextcloud WebDAV mount refused the `.part` file name, and that only showed up in rclone's log. #866 was opened in 2024 for the same reason (IOErrors on files that were fine) but was closed without tests.

The message now includes the `OSError` and drops the guess:

```
ERROR    IOError while writing file to .../IMG_7409.JPG: [Errno 28] No space left on device. Skipping this file...
```

The two existing tests (`test_handle_io_error` and `test_handle_io_error_name_id7`) raised a bare `IOError`. They now raise an `OSError` with an errno (`ENOSPC` in one, `EINVAL` in the other) and check that it appears in the message. Both fail on master. Full suite (in UTC and in my local time zone), ruff and mypy `--strict` pass.

This doesn't change the `.part` suffix that #1288 asks about. That's a separate decision, but with this change the next person with the same problem will see the error.

issue.body:
Fixes #40217

CODEOWNERS review requests were created for every user and team listed in the file, even if they can't read the repo. On a private repo that means outsiders get added as reviewers and get notified about a PR they can't open, while the reviewer picker in the UI (and the manual review request API) would never allow it.

`pullRequestCodeOwnersReview` now runs the same checks `isValidReviewRequest` / `isValidTeamReviewRequest` use for manual requests:

- a user is only requested if they have read access to the pull requests unit
- on a private repo, a team is only requested if the repo is assigned to it

Anyone skipped is just left out; the rest of the code owners are still requested as before.

I didn't try to restrict public repos to collaborators/team members only. Manual requests allow any user who can read a public repo today, so I kept the two paths consistent. Happy to tighten that if you'd prefer it to match the UI picker exactly.

## Testing

Added `TestPullRequestCodeOwnersReviewSkipsReviewersWithoutAccess` (private org3/repo3, with a non-member user and an org team that doesn't have the repo). It fails on main (both outsiders get requested) and passes with the fix:

    go test -count=1 -run 'TestPullRequestCodeOwnersReview' ./services/issue/

`go test ./services/issue/... ./services/pull/... ./models/issues/...` passes.

I used an AI coding assistant to help write this change. I've reviewed and tested it myself.

issue.title: `rtk ls` takes flag values for paths: `-I PATTERN` becomes a path operand, `-Ihello` is sent as `-Ieo`
issue.body:
## What happens

`rtk ls` splits its arguments into flags and paths on a leading `-` alone, so it gets wrong any flag that takes a value.

- **Separate value:** the value is treated as a path and moved after the flags. `rtk ls -I '*.md' -R src/core` runs `ls -l -I -R *.md src/core`. `-R` becomes the ignore pattern, `*.md` becomes a path operand, and the command exits 2. `README.md` is listed although `-I '*.md'` asked to hide it.
- **Attached value:** the short-flag cluster is rebuilt by removing every `l`, `a` and `h` character, value included. `-Ihello` is sent as `-Ieo`. The same test also sets the long-listing detection, which looks for `l`/`g`/`n`/`o` anywhere in a short cluster.

## Reproduce

```bash
export LC_ALL=C
mkdir -p repro/src/core/sub && cd repro
touch src/core/a.rs src/core/README.md src/core/sub/b.rs

rtk ls -I '*.md' -R src/core; echo "rc=$?"
# src/core:
# total 4
# -rw-rw-r-- 1 user user    0 ... README.md
# -rw-rw-r-- 1 user user    0 ... a.rs
# drwxrwxr-x 2 user user 4096 ... sub
# ls: cannot access '*.md': No such file or directory
# rc=2

ls -l -I '*.md' -R src/core; echo "rc=$?"
# src/core:
# total 4
# -rw-rw-r-- 1 user user    0 ... a.rs
# drwxrwxr-x 2 user user 4096 ... sub
# (and src/core/sub)
# rc=0
```

The attached form (`-Ihello` → `-Ieo`) follows from the cluster rebuild in `src/cmds/system/ls.rs` (`run`: the `flags`/`paths` partition and the `filter(|c| *c != 'l' && *c != 'a' && *c != 'h')` loop).

## Expected

Flag values stay attached to their flags, whether separate (`-I PATTERN`, `--hide PATTERN`, `-w COLS`, `-T COLS`, `--block-size SIZE`, `--sort WORD`, `--time WORD`, `--format WORD`, …) or attached (`-Ihello`, `--ignore=*.md`). A value is never taken for a path, and never edited by the cluster rebuild. Parsing through `arg_tokenizer` with ls's value table gives that.

## Related

#3608 (`-a` handling) and #4302 (`-t` ordering) are other `rtk ls` flag problems, but neither covers flag values.

issue.title: rtk git commit silently drops a literal -- pathspec separator before invoking git
issue.body:
### Summary
`rtk git commit -- <file> -F <path>` silently drops the literal `--` pathspec separator before invoking real `git`. This changes argument-parsing semantics: with `--` present, git treats everything after it as literal pathspecs (so `-F <path>` would itself be a pathspec, not a flag); with `--` silently removed, `-F <path>` is instead parsed as git's `--file` flag (read commit message from file).

### Environment
- rtk 0.42.3 and 0.45.0, Windows (Git-Bash)
- Invoked both via the Claude Code PreToolUse hook (`rtk hook claude`) and directly as `rtk git commit …`

### To reproduce
In any git repo with a staged file `foo.txt`:
```
rtk git commit -- foo.txt -F /absolute/path/outside/repo/msg.txt
```

### Expected
Matches native `git commit -- foo.txt -F /absolute/path/outside/repo/msg.txt`:
```
fatal: /absolute/path/outside/repo/msg.txt: '/absolute/path/outside/repo/msg.txt' is outside repository at '<repo>'
```
(exit 128) — with `--` present, `-F` and its argument are literal pathspecs, and an absolute path outside the repo is rejected.

### Actual
rtk commits cleanly, using the file's contents as the commit message — it silently dropped `--` before calling git, so `-F` got reinterpreted as git's own `--file` flag instead of staying a pathspec.

### Evidence it's rtk's arg handling, not git
- Native `git commit -- foo.txt -F <path>` (no rtk) → reliably reproduces the `outside repository` error, confirmed across 1-file and 3-file pathspec lists, POSIX and Windows-backslash paths.
- `rtk git commit -- foo.txt -F <path>` → always succeeds cleanly instead, on both 0.42.3 and 0.45.0.
- rtk's own tracking DB (`history.db`) logs the rewritten/executed command without the `--` that was actually typed.

### Impact
Any `git commit … -- <pathspecs> …` invocation containing flag-like tokens after `--` behaves differently under rtk than under raw git — silent semantic drift rather than a passthrough match, which runs counter to rtk's own fallback/compatibility goals for git subcommands.

### Related
#2454 (open) is a different bug in the same general area — `git stash push -- <path>` gets a malformed pathspec-magic prefix injected (`:(,prefix:0)`) rather than a dropped separator. Distinct root cause and reproduction, but both point at rtk's `--` / pathspec handling being subcommand-inconsistent across `commit` and `stash push`.

Pulled this locally and tested it. The 10 tests in `post-bash-command-log.test.js` pass, and `node tests/run-all.js` gives 8297/8301. The 4 failures are the real-scanner cases in `codex-hooks.test.js`, which fail the same way on main for me.

issue.title: Downloads hang indefinitely — streaming asset download has no read timeout
issue.body:
## Overview

On large libraries, downloads hang indefinitely on a random asset. I think the root cause is that the streaming asset download has no read timeout, so a half-open connection blocks forever and the existing retry logic never fires. Follow-up to the symptoms in #1257 and #1196.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. icloudpd **1.32.3**, macOS **26.3** (Python 3.13), downloading a large-ish library.
2. Run a full sync, e.g. `icloudpd --username <redacted> --directory ./photos --size original`
3. Let it run — on a large library it eventually wedges on a random asset (small files included): 0 bytes for 10+ minutes, no error. `lsof`/`netstat` shows the connection in `CLOSE_WAIT`. Killing and restarting resumes… until it stalls on another asset.

(It's intermittent — it depends on a connection going half-open, which is server-side/timing dependent — but the missing timeout is a latent bug regardless of when it triggers.)

## Expected Behavior

A stalled download should **time out and retry** (or fail cleanly) so the run keeps making progress unattended — not block forever requiring manual kill/restart.

## Actual Behavior

The download parks indefinitely with no error and no retry. In `src/pyicloud_ipd/services/photos.py`:

```python
def download_asset(session, url, start=0):
    headers = {"Range": f"bytes={start}-"}
    return session.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True)   # no timeout=
```

There's no `timeout=`, and with `stream=True` the bytes are read later while iterating the response. If the connection half-opens mid-stream, that read blocks forever — `requests` never raises, so the retry logic (which looks for `ConnectionError` / `socket.timeout`) never gets a chance to fire.

## Context

This is what forces the "restart it 20–30 times over 6 hours" experience reported in #1257 — it turns an unattended backup into constant babysitting. The fix looks small:

1. Pass `timeout=(connect, read)` to that `get()`; with `stream=True` the read value bounds each chunk read, so a stall raises `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout` instead of hanging.
2. Have the download retry path also catch `requests.exceptions.Timeout` (`ReadTimeout` isn't a `ConnectionError`, so I don't think it's retried as-is).
3. Expose it as a `--download-timeout` option with a sane default.

Per CONTRIBUTING I wanted to raise this before opening a PR — happy to write it up with a test that mocks a read timeout and asserts it retries. Does this direction seem right?

comment.body:
I checked this against the code. This request does have a timeout: `PyiCloudSession.request` adds `timeout` to every call that doesn't pass one ([session.py#L75-L76](https://github.com/icloud-photos-downloader/icloud_photos_downloader/blob/ae0e84e7e859f527bd6923c7dc7934b9f3295ac6/src/pyicloud_ipd/session.py#L75-L76)), and `http_timeout` defaults to 30 seconds. That came with #1114 in 1.27.5, so 1.32.3 has it, and `download_asset` goes through that session.

With `stream=True` the timeout applies to each read while the body is streamed. I tried it with a local server that sends the headers and 100 bytes and then stops sending: `iter_content` raises `requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: Read timed out` once the timeout has passed. In 1.32.3 that error is caught by `except OSError` (requests exceptions subclass `IOError`), so the file is skipped with the "IOError while writing file" message and the run goes on. On master, since #1436, it's handled as a dropped connection and the download resumes from the `.part` file.

So a stalled read on the download connection shouldn't block forever. A connection in `CLOSE_WAIT` also means Apple already closed its side, and reading from it returns right away, so the process is probably waiting somewhere else. A stack dump of the stuck process would show where: `pip install py-spy`, then `sudo py-spy dump --pid <pid>` while it hangs. If you can post that output, it should point to the right place.

issue.title: Three-way merge when a file changed in the project since the session started
issue.body:
Asked on the Product Hunt page: two agents run in two Mudroom sessions on the same project and both edit the same file. The first apply goes through. The second apply then reports that file as a conflict ("project changed since the session started") and leaves it alone, while the other files of that session still apply. Today the only way forward is to merge the file by hand.

Every session keeps the base version the agent started from, so Mudroom has all three sides for a normal three-way merge: base, the project as it is now, and the session's copy.

Possible shape:

- During apply, for a text file in conflict, try a three-way merge of base, project and work.
- If it merges cleanly, show the merged result in the review as its own entry and apply it like any other change, with undo.
- If it doesn't, write nothing and keep today's conflict, maybe with the merge markers available to copy.
- Binary files, symlinks, mode changes and deletions stay as they are now (conflict, apply by hand).

Hunk apply needs the same check, since a hunk from the session can still land cleanly when the project changed in a different part of the file.

1. A class in `src/data/kucoin.ts` that implements `DataSource` from `src/data/types.ts`. `src/data/okx.ts` and `src/data/bybit.ts` are the closest examples: symbol search, history paging to the left, and live updates.

comment.body:

issue.title: Add ta.sar (Parabolic SAR) to Kandle Script
issue.body:
The chart already has a Parabolic SAR indicator (`SAR` in `src/chart/indicators.ts`), but scripts can't compute it: `ta.sar(start, inc, max)` is missing from Kandle Script.

`ta.sar` follows the usual rules: the stop starts at the previous extreme, moves toward price by the acceleration factor times the distance to the extreme point, the factor starts at `start`, grows by `inc` each time a new extreme is made and is capped at `max`, and the trend flips when price crosses the stop.

Where to start:

- `src/script/builtins/ta.ts` for the built-in. It needs per-call state (current trend, extreme point, acceleration factor), like `ta.supertrend`.
- The test in `tests/script/ta.test.ts` called "agrees with the chart helpers" compares script built-ins with the chart's own calculations in `src/chart/ta.ts`. If the chart's SAR uses the same rules, add a line there too; if the two differ, write down why in the pull request.
- Add a reference version to `tests/script/reference.ts` and list `ta.sar` in the README.

`pnpm test` and `pnpm build` must pass.

issue.title: Add ta.cmo and ta.tsi to Kandle Script
issue.body:
Two momentum oscillators are missing from Kandle Script: the Chande Momentum Oscillator and the True Strength Index.

- `ta.cmo(source, length)`: over the last `length` bars, sum the positive changes (`up`) and the absolute negative changes (`down`) of `source`, then return `100 * (up - down) / (up + down)`.
- `ta.tsi(source, short_length, long_length)`: double-smooth the one-bar change with EMAs (`long_length` first, then `short_length`), do the same for its absolute value, and return the ratio. It returns a value between -1 and 1, not a percentage.

Where to start:

- `src/script/builtins/ta.ts`. `ta.rsi` and `ta.mom` already track bar-to-bar changes, and `ta.ema` shows how a smoothed value keeps its state.
- Add whole-array reference versions to `tests/script/reference.ts` and a check for each in `tests/script/ta.test.ts`. Include a case where `source` is flat, so `up + down` is 0, and decide what it returns (`na` is fine; say so in a comment).
- List both in the README under "What is supported".

One pull request for both is fine. `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` must pass.

issue.title: Add ta.swma, ta.range and ta.kcw to Kandle Script
issue.body:
These three are short and make a good first contribution to the script runtime:

- `ta.swma(source)`: symmetrically weighted moving average over 4 bars, weights 1/6, 2/6, 2/6, 1/6.
- `ta.range(source, length)`: highest minus lowest value of `source` over the last `length` bars.
- `ta.kcw(source, length, mult)`: Keltner Channel width, `(upper - lower) / middle`. `ta.kc` already returns the three lines, so this can reuse it.

Where to start:

- `src/script/builtins/ta.ts`. `ta.bbw` is the closest example for `ta.kcw`, and the `highest` / `lowest` helpers (`windowExtreme`) fit `ta.range`.
- Add reference versions to `tests/script/reference.ts` and checks to `tests/script/ta.test.ts`.
- Add them to the README list under "What is supported".

Feel free to take just one of them. Say which in a comment so two people don't do the same one.

issue.title: Add ta.alma to Kandle Script
issue.body:
Kandle Script has `ta.sma`, `ta.ema`, `ta.wma`, `ta.hma` and `ta.vwma`, but not the Arnaud Legoux moving average. Scripts that call `ta.alma(source, length, offset, sigma)` fail with an unknown-function error.

`ta.alma` weights the last `length` values with a Gaussian curve centred at `offset * (length - 1)`, with width `length / sigma`. The weights are normalised so they sum to 1. Most definitions also accept an optional fifth argument, `floor`, which floors the offset before computing the weights.

Where to start:

- The `ta.*` built-ins are in `src/script/builtins/ta.ts`. `ta.wma` is a close model: it keeps the source history in its state and recomputes the window on each bar.
- Add a plain whole-array version to `tests/script/reference.ts` and a `check('ta.alma(close, 9, 0.85, 6)', ref.alma(close, 9, 0.85, 6))` line to the moving averages test in `tests/script/ta.test.ts`.
- Add it to the `ta.*` list under "What is supported" in the README.

Write it from the formula, not from another product's code (see CONTRIBUTING.md). `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` must pass.
